- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then gradually converges toward true values — suggest adjusting initial forecast upward by 1–2% for short-term (0–5 day) windows.
- After sharp spikes in true values (e.g., 51.06, 53.86), model tends to overshoot and stay elevated for 3–5 days — apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 1–3% after peak, then allow gradual mean reversion.
- Model underestimates true values in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day window — consider adding a 0.5–1.5% upward bias for the last 5 days to capture tail risk or lagged market reactions.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values (mean forecast > true mean by 1.5–3%) — apply a global downward shift of 1.2–1.8% to align with historical mean reversion.
- Model fails to capture sudden downward corrections (e.g., 53.86 → 47.05) — introduce a “sudden drop” trigger: if true value drops >3% from prior day, reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 3 days.
- Model overfits recent high volatility — avoid extrapolating from recent spikes; use 30-day rolling mean as a baseline for smoothing out short-term noise.
